correctness.rationale: The four-edge cost budget is exactly the weighted sum of two Rayleigh energies for h=sqrt(t)<=3, giving the universal spectral gap upper bound 4/(h²+2h+5). The displayed feasible rates satisfy both eigenvector equations; the trace identifies the fourth eigenvalue and spectral separation, and equality with two strictly positive multipliers for h<3 yields uniqueness. For t>=9 the fixed vector (3,-3,-1,1) gives the universal bound 1/5-(t-9)q/5. Its equality cases yield the unique high-cost path and the complete critical affine family; exact remaining eigenvalues impose q in [0,1/15]. Exact-rational checker verifies the characteristic polynomials for 12 interior/endpoint parameter values, 41 boundary cases and 5 exterior choices. The infinite-parameter result rests on the analytic inequalities rather than on finite checks.

originality.rationale: The novel claim assessed is the exact full cost-parametric optimizer set and nine-price transition for a four-cycle, not the previously known SDP formulation or equal-cost cycle case. Primary full text of Sun et al. 2006 (Sections 1, 5.2, 5.3) gives arbitrary-cost paths, equal-cost cycles, and only a two-dimensional embedding statement for general-cost cycles; no cost-ratio-nine optimizer family. The relevant sections of Shakeri et al. define a fixed-layer interlink-only optimization, which is not the same four-free-rate heterogeneous-cost family. Exact scientific-query searches in published research records and scholarly indexes did not return this statement, but cannot establish universal novelty. value.rationale: The four-cycle is a small, natural even-cycle topology with a removable shortcut while retaining connected diffusion; the one-price family probes precisely when purchasing that shortcut improves optimal mixing. The theorem gives an exact global edge-allocation policy, a sharp support/deletion threshold at nine, a nonunique critical optimal face, and a change of spectral-gap multiplicity. These data directly resolve a meaningful parametric network-design problem without a numerical SDP solve, and are not simply a known generic solver restatement or an unmotivated isolated numerical example.
